_comment: The showrunner's episode plan for the kids biology module of story_screenplay_module.json (#2680): what the plan call answers. Planning fields in English; titles, discoveries, card titles and catchphrases in both languages. Refs q1..q12 are the module quiz's questions as the plan prompt numbers them.
logline: {child} and {friend} must sort Grandma Mariam's basket of treasures into living and not living for Friday's science fair, but a shy snail keeps escaping and a rival team says the mimosa only moves in the wind.
want: Win the living-or-not table at Friday's science fair with Grandma's basket.
stakes: Grandma promised her sweetest mangoes to the whole class if the table wins.
clock: The fair opens on Friday morning.
hero_flaw: {child} rushes to an answer before looking.

voices.hero: rushes, then catches the mistake and works it out out loud
voices.friend: names every object, jumps to wild theories, loves riddles
voices.mentor: answers a question with a question, lends the microscope
voices.family: teases kindly, proud of her basket and her mangoes
voices.margo: whispers one riddle-like hint, never the answer

running_gag: The shy snail keeps escaping and leaves a silver trail.

chapters.opens_on: Grandma Mariam tips her basket of treasures onto the courtyard bench.
chapters.goal: Sort Grandma's treasures into living and not living for the fair table.
chapters.obstacle: {child} rushes and calls the hiding snail dead.

beats.problem: The snail and the mimosa sprig lie still: are they alive?

discovery.en: The leaf folds when you touch it: living things react!
discovery.fr: La feuille se ferme quand on la touche : le vivant réagit !

beats.problem: The néré seed does nothing at all: is it dead like the pebble?

discovery.en: A seed feeds, grows and makes new seeds: it is alive, just asleep!
discovery.fr: Une graine se nourrit, grandit et refait des graines : elle vit, elle dort !

beats.problem: The seed and the pebble look the same to the eye.

discovery.en: The seed is full of tiny boxes, the pebble has none: life has cells!
discovery.fr: La graine est pleine de petites boîtes, le caillou non : le vivant a des cellules !

chapters.turn: Under Mr Kaboré's microscope the néré seed shows tiny cells and the pebble shows none.
chapters.ends_on: The snail is gone; a silver trail runs under the classroom door.
chapters.paper_task: the living-or-not list for the fair table

chapters.opens_on: Monday: the silver trail ends on a bean leaf in the school garden.
chapters.goal: Explain to the jury how a tiny snail is built, from cell to whole animal.
chapters.obstacle: {friend} insists the whole snail is one giant cell.

beats.problem: {friend} says the snail is one giant cell.

discovery.en: One cell is the smallest living piece: a snail has millions!
discovery.fr: Une cellule est le plus petit morceau vivant : un escargot en a des millions !

card_title.fr: Le plus petit bout de vie

beats.problem: A bean leaf under the microscope looks like a wall of green bricks.

discovery.en: Same cells side by side make a tissue, and tissues make a leaf!
discovery.fr: Des cellules pareilles font un tissu, et les tissus font une feuille !

beats.problem: How do all these parts crawl like one animal?

discovery.en: Organs team up in systems, and the systems make one whole snail!
discovery.fr: Les organes font équipe en systèmes, et ça fait un escargot entier !

chapters.turn: {child} climbs the ladder from cell to tissue, organ, system and snail.
chapters.ends_on: Grandma calls: the rival team says the mimosa only folds because of the wind.
chapters.game: sort the cards from cell to organism before the bell
chapters.paper_task: draw the ladder from cell to snail for the fair poster

chapters.opens_on: A rival poster on Grandma's gate says MIMOSA = WIND.
chapters.goal: Prove that the mimosa folds because it is touched, not because of the wind.
chapters.obstacle: {child} wants to fan the plant and touch it at the same time.

beats.problem: Everyone shouts a reason; nobody has looked at the plant.

discovery.en: First we look closely, then we ask one clear question.
discovery.fr: D'abord on regarde de près, puis on pose une seule question claire.

beats.problem: Wild guesses fly: a ghost, the wind, magic.

discovery.en: Our guess is that touch makes it fold, and we can test that!
discovery.fr: Notre idée : le toucher la fait se fermer, et on peut le tester !

beats.problem: {child} wants to fan and touch the mimosa at once.

discovery.en: Two pots, same sun, same water: only one thing changes!
discovery.fr: Deux pots, même soleil, même eau : une seule chose change !

chapters.turn: With two mimosa pots, only the touched one folds: touch, not wind.
chapters.ends_on: Friday dawn: the basket waits on the fair table, but the snail has escaped again.
chapters.paper_task: the fair-test plan: what changes and what stays the same

rally.opens_on: The jury walks toward the fair table and the snail is missing.
rally.final_obstacle: The jury wants proof, object by object, of what is alive, and one juror doubts the mimosa test.

steps.uses: react and cells: the shy snail hides, the pebble has no cells
the ladder poster from cell to snail
a fair test, and a new guess when a test says no

rally.resolution: {child} follows the silver trail to the snail and proves, card by card, what is alive; the jury pins a golden ribbon.
rally.last_image: {friend} ties a tiny ribbon on the pebble: best non-living friend.
